entities.summary: Richard de Beauchamp, 13th Earl of Warwick, was a pivotal figure in medieval English history, playing a crucial role in the Wars of the Roses. Born into a noble family, he became a prominent military commander and politician, vying for power with rival claimants to the throne. His strategic alliances and tactical victories earned him a reputation as a skilled leader, while his personal life was marked by turmoil, including a high-profile marriage to Joan Radcliffe. Despite his efforts to secure his family's legacy, de Beauchamp's fortunes waned, and he ultimately died in 1439, leaving behind a complex and contested legacy. The intricate web of alliances and rivalries he navigated had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of English history for generations to come. As the last scion of the powerful Beauchamp family, de Beauchamp's story serves as a testament to the enduring power of family, loyalty, and the struggle for power in the treacherous landscape of medieval politics. In the annals of English history, de Beauchamp's name remains synonymous with the tumultuous era of the Wars of the Roses, a period marked by bloodshed, betrayal, and the ruthless pursuit of power. As the 13th Earl of Warwick, de Beauchamp's influence extended far beyond his own family's fortunes, leaving an indelible mark on the course of English history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Richard de Beauchamp, 13th Earl of Warwick, played a significant role in shaping the course of English history during the Wars of the Roses. His military victories and strategic alliances helped to secure the loyalty of key nobles and armies, contributing to the Lancastrian cause. Despite his efforts to secure his family's legacy, de Beauchamp's fortunes waned, and he ultimately died in 1439, leaving behind a complex and contested legacy. The intricate web of alliances and rivalries he navigated had far-reaching consequences, shaping the fate of the Lancastrian and Yorkist causes.
